name: tModLoader-Web-Managed-Server
description: Run a modded Terraria dedicated server with a web dashboard for worlds, Workshop mods, players, settings, backups, and restart schedules. First startup needs internet access. Find the one-time setup code in the container logs, then open WebUI to create your administrator credential. Use dedicated data and backup folders, and keep the dashboard on a trusted LAN or behind an HTTPS reverse proxy. See the README for installation and configuration. Independently maintained; not affiliated with Re-Logic or the tModLoader team.

paths.name: Server data
paths.description: Dedicated folder for worlds, mods, runtime, dashboard credentials, settings, and logs. Startup sets ownership to 1000:1000. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Updates-and-Storage#persistent-folders

paths.name: Backup archives
paths.description: Dedicated backup folder. Preserve this and server data during updates. Startup sets ownership to 1000:1000. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Updates-and-Storage#persistent-folders

ports.name: Game port
ports.description: Host TCP port players connect to. Keep the container port at 7777. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Networking-and-Access#game-connections

ports.name: Dashboard port
ports.description: Host dashboard port. Keep the container port at 8080; the WebUI button follows this mapping. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Networking-and-Access#change-the-dashboard-port

variables.name: Manage game settings with
variables.description: web: saved dashboard values override Unraid game settings; Unraid values only seed unsaved settings. env: Unraid controls game settings and dashboard configuration editing is disabled. Dashboard disabled always uses env. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#choose-who-manages-settings

variables.name: Use custom server configuration
variables.description: Yes requires TMOD_CONFIG_SOURCE=env or dashboard disabled, plus a separately added read-only file mapping to /terraria-server/customconfig.txt. Keep its game port at 7777 for this template. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#custom-server-configuration

variables.name: Dashboard origin
variables.description: Leave empty for server-IP access. For a hostname or proxy, enter the exact browser origin including scheme and non-default port. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#web-dashboard

variables.name: Trusted proxy
variables.description: Optional single proxy IP or DNS name as seen by the container. Proxy must overwrite forwarding headers; see networking documentation. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#web-dashboard

variables.name: Administrator hash file
variables.description: WebUI only. Optional container path to an existing Argon2id credential hash file; add a matching read-only file mount. Empty uses first-run setup. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#web-dashboard

variables.name: Workshop API key file
variables.description: WebUI only. Optional container path to a Steam API key file; add a matching read-only file mount. A key saved in the dashboard takes precedence. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#web-dashboard

variables.name: Game password file
variables.description: Optional path inside the container; add a matching read-only file mount. Saved dashboard passwords override this in web mode. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#change-the-game-password

variables.name: Automatic runtime updates
variables.description: 1 checks and tests runtime updates at startup. 0 retains the installed runtime. First startup always requires a download. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#startup-runtime-updates

variables.name: Runtime update channel
variables.description: Empty follows the image channel; enter stable or preview to override. Applied at container startup. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#startup-runtime-updates

variables.name: Runtime version pin
variables.description: Exact supported tModLoader release. Empty follows the selected channel; downgrades require a matching checkpoint. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#startup-runtime-updates

variables.name: Update free-space reserve (MiB)
variables.description: Additional free space beyond three copies of game data required for startup update staging. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#startup-runtime-updates

variables.name: Update readiness timeout (seconds)
variables.description: Maximum wait for the copied-world compatibility test and live startup readiness. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#startup-runtime-updates

variables.name: GitHub API token
variables.description: Optional narrowly scoped token for release-discovery API rate limits. Not required for ordinary public downloads. Stored in container configuration; not a dashboard setting. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Updates-and-Storage#startup-runtime-updates

variables.name: Enable Dashboard
variables.description: Enabled (1): no need to set any game settings below; leave their defaults and configure them in the dashboard. Keep Manage game settings with set to web (default). Optional deployment settings above are configured in Unraid. Disabled (0): expand Show more settings and configure the game settings in Unraid; administrator setup is skipped. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#web-dashboard

variables.name: Initial game password
variables.description: Optional player password, separate from the administrator credential. Empty disables it. Saved dashboard password overrides this after setup. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#change-the-game-password

variables.name: Welcome message
variables.value: A tModLoader server powered by Docker!
variables.description: Message displayed to players when they join the server. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#game-network-and-access

variables.name: Maximum players
variables.description: Maximum simultaneous players allowed, from 1 to 255. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#game-network-and-access

variables.name: Server language
variables.description: Language code for server messages, such as en-US. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#game-network-and-access

variables.name: Additional cheat protection
variables.description: 0 disables Terraria’s additional cheat checks; 1 enables them. This is not authentication or a firewall. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

variables.name: NPC streaming range
variables.description: Controls NPC streaming to clients, from 0 to 1000. Leave the default unless tuning network behavior. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

variables.name: UPnP port mapping
variables.description: 0 disables automatic router port mapping; 1 requests it. Docker port publishing and firewall rules still need host configuration. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

variables.name: World name
variables.description: Selects the world file by name. A different name may create a new world if no matching file exists. Do not include path separators. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#world-selection-and-generation

variables.name: New world size
variables.description: Used only when creating a world: 1 small, 2 medium, 3 large. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#world-selection-and-generation

variables.name: New world evil
variables.description: Random, Corruption, or Crimson. To change evil in the WebUI, choose an unused world name, stage the settings, and apply changes. Apply saves and stops the game, disconnects players, creates the new world, and restarts. Existing worlds are never converted; a matching name loads that world. Custom evil requires a name of at most 26 characters and seed of at most 39 characters. Special seeds and mods may generate both evils or alter generation. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#world-selection-and-generation

variables.name: New world seed
variables.description: Seed used when generating a new world. Changing it does not regenerate the current world. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#world-selection-and-generation

variables.name: New world difficulty
variables.description: Used when creating a world: 0 Classic, 1 Expert, 2 Master, 3 Journey. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#world-selection-and-generation

variables.name: Selected Workshop entries
variables.description: Comma-separated Workshop mod IDs or collection:ID entries. Removing an entry disables it on managed startup but keeps cached downloads. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#mods-and-workshop

variables.name: Steam offline policy
variables.description: use-cache allows startup with available cached mods when Steam cannot be reached. strict fails if required update/download checks fail. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#mods-and-workshop

variables.name: Collection expansion limit
variables.description: Maximum items allowed while expanding Workshop collections, from 1 to 1000. Limits unexpectedly large collections. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#mods-and-workshop

variables.name: Download attempts
variables.description: Maximum attempts for transient Steam Workshop download failures, from 1 to 20. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#mods-and-workshop

variables.name: Retry delay (seconds)
variables.description: Time to wait between failed download attempts, from 0 to 600 seconds. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#mods-and-workshop

variables.name: Autosave interval (minutes)
variables.description: Save the live world every N minutes (default: 10). 0 disables scheduled autosaves. Saves update the world in place without disconnecting players; they do not create backup archives. Save the draft, then Apply & Restart to activate a changed interval. The timer resets when the game starts. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

variables.name: Autosave chat announcement
variables.description: Chat message sent before each scheduled save. Leave empty to save silently. The autosave interval controls the schedule; 0 disables scheduled saves. Save the draft and apply to activate changes. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

variables.name: Backup schedule
variables.description: Choose disabled, minutes, every X days, daily, weekly, or monthly. Interval mode preserves the existing backup interval. Cold backups disconnect players, save, archive, and restart the game. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

variables.name: Backup interval (minutes)
variables.description: 0 disables scheduled backups. 1440 runs approximately every 24 hours. The interval resets on container start or after a manual backup. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

variables.name: Back up every X days
variables.description: Used in days mode. Each day is 24 hours. The timer resets on container startup, configuration apply, and after any backup attempt. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

variables.name: Backup weekday
variables.description: Used for weekly backups at the selected backup time and timezone. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

variables.name: Backup day of month
variables.description: Used for monthly backups. Choose 1 through 31; shorter months use their last day. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

variables.name: Backup time
variables.description: Daily, weekly, and monthly backups use this 24-hour HH:MM time. Busy or unhealthy servers defer the backup. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

variables.name: Backup timezone
variables.description: Use UTC or an IANA timezone such as America/New_York. Missing daylight-saving times shift forward; repeated times use their first occurrence. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

variables.name: Backups to retain
variables.description: Number of verified backup bundles to keep for this data directory. Cleanup runs only after a successful backup and restart; recovery originals are not pruned. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

variables.name: Minimum free space (MiB)
variables.description: Refuse a backup before stopping the game when /backups has less free space than this threshold. 1024 means 1 GiB. This is not an archive-size estimate; 0 disables the threshold. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

variables.name: Restart schedule
variables.description: Choose disabled (default), minutes, every X days, daily, weekly, or monthly. Save the draft and apply to activate changes. Busy or unhealthy servers defer the restart until ready. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

variables.name: Restart interval (minutes)
variables.description: Used in interval mode only. 0 disables interval restarts; 1440 is approximately every 24 hours. The timer resets whenever the game starts, including after backups or applying settings. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

variables.name: Restart every X days
variables.description: Used in every-X-days mode. Enter 1 through 3650; each day is exactly 24 hours. The timer resets whenever the game starts, including after backups or applying settings. It does not use the calendar time or timezone. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

variables.name: Restart weekday
variables.description: Used in weekly mode. Choose the weekday on which the restart warning begins, at the selected time in the selected timezone. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

variables.name: Restart day of month
variables.description: Used in monthly mode. Choose 1 through 31. If a month has fewer days, use its last day: 31 becomes February 28 or 29, for example. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

variables.name: Restart time
variables.description: Used for daily, weekly, and monthly schedules. Enter HH:MM in 24-hour format, such as 04:00, in the restart timezone below. The warning starts at this time; the game stops after the warning delay. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

variables.name: Restart timezone
variables.description: Used for daily, weekly, and monthly schedules. Use UTC or an IANA timezone such as America/New_York. A skipped daylight-saving time shifts forward by the clock-change gap; a repeated time runs at its first occurrence only. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

variables.name: Restart warning delay (seconds)
variables.description: Wait after the scheduled restart announcement before saving and stopping the game. Default: 60; 0 restarts immediately. This delay is separate from the Docker shutdown warning delay. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

variables.name: Restart countdown warnings (seconds)
variables.description: Comma-separated remaining times, such as 300,60,10. Warnings longer than the restart delay are skipped. Leave empty to disable countdown chat messages; the initial announcement is controlled separately. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

variables.name: Restart chat announcement
variables.value: Scheduled server restart soon. Please prepare to disconnect.
variables.description: Chat message sent when a scheduled restart becomes due, before the warning delay. Leave empty to omit the announcement. Players will still disconnect when the game restarts. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

variables.name: Shutdown announcement
variables.description: Chat message sent to players when Docker requests a graceful container shutdown. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

variables.name: Shutdown warning delay (seconds)
variables.description: Wait after the shutdown announcement before requesting save-and-exit when Docker stops the container. Default: 3; 0 skips the delay. Keep Docker stop_grace_period longer than this delay plus the graceful shutdown timeout and shutdown overhead. Dashboard restarts and backups use their own stop flow. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. Keep Unraid Docker Stop Timeout and Extra Parameters --stop-timeout greater than shutdown delay + timeout + overhead (120 seconds by default). || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

variables.name: Graceful shutdown timeout (seconds)
variables.description: How long to wait after requesting a save-and-exit before forced termination. Keep Docker’s stop_grace_period longer than this value plus shutdown overhead. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. Keep Unraid Docker Stop Timeout and Extra Parameters --stop-timeout greater than shutdown delay + timeout + overhead (120 seconds by default). || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

variables.name: Console verbosity
variables.description: quiet reduces routine output; normal shows standard output; debug shows detailed output. Complete raw output remains in the persistent console log. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

variables.name: Crash replay lines
variables.description: Number of raw console lines replayed when the game fails. 0 disables crash replay; debug already shows raw output. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

variables.name: Console history retention (days)
variables.description: Remove archived console logs older than this many days. Default: 30; 0 disables age-based cleanup. The current and previous console logs and tModLoader own logs are kept. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

variables.name: Console history size limit (MiB)
variables.description: Remove oldest archived console logs until history fits this budget. Default: 512; 0 disables the size limit. Current and previous console logs are separate from this budget. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

variables.name: Console log rotation size (MiB)
variables.description: Rotate the current console log at this size so one long server session cannot grow it indefinitely. Default: 64. Cleanup runs at startup, rotation, and periodically while output is received. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

variables.name: Process priority
variables.description: Server scheduling priority, from 0 (realtime) to 5 (idle). Lower values request higher priority; container permissions may limit this. Prefer the default unless diagnosing performance. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

variables.name: Freeze time
variables.description: Who can control freeze time in a Journey world: 0 locked, 1 host only, 2 everyone. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#journey-permissions

variables.description: Who can control rain strength in a Journey world: 0 locked, 1 host only, 2 everyone. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#journey-permissions

variables.description: Who can control time speed in a Journey world: 0 locked, 1 host only, 2 everyone. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#journey-permissions

variables.description: Who can control freeze rain in a Journey world: 0 locked, 1 host only, 2 everyone. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#journey-permissions
